newsitem.title: USA: Cephalon holds to year-end goal for NDAs.
newsitem.headline: Cephalon holds to year-end goal for NDAs.

text.p: Cephalon Inc chief executive Frank Baldino reiterated on Wednesday the company's goal of filing its Myotrophin and Provigil drugs with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by the end of the year.
Baldino told a Robertson Stephens medical conference the company hoped to file a New Drug Application for Myotrophin "as soon as possible."
"The goal has always been the end of this year and I think we'll be very close to that goal," he said.
The FDA in June approved a program granting patients suffering from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, or Lou Gehrig's disease, early access to the drug ahead of final marketing approval by the agency.

The early access program approval came after FDA officials questioned during an independent advisory panel meeting whether or not data from a European trial supported the finding of a North American trial that showed the drug reduced the severity and slowed the progression of ALS.
Cephalon has partnered with Chiron Corp for Myotrophin.
Baldino said the company plans to file Provigil, for treating excessive daytime sleepiness associated with narcolepsy, "as soon as possibile, hopefully by the end of the year."
